source_text: Igitur et secundum te in adoptione quidem per omnes aetates gratiae est aequalis effectus; in remissione vero peccatorum non in omnibus est una taxatio. Sed egi hactenus parce nimis atque patienter.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore even according to you in adoption indeed through all ages there is an equal effect of grace; but in the remission of sins there is not in all one taxation. But I have acted until now too sparingly and patiently.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'

pass_b_english: Thus, even according to you, grace has an equal effect in adoption throughout every age; but in the remission of sins the reckoning is not the same for everyone. Yet so far I have acted far too sparingly and patiently.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
In this book Julian usually means the Savior's gift abounding against Adam's sin (Rom 5), not later system-grace as a substance, and not 'favoritism' unless a suum-cuique definition is in play.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
